question: Should Workboard retain manual operator acceptance for `done`, with stronger diagnostics and structured evidence, or should it become an enforcement point that rejects completion based on proof, dependency, and external pull-request conditions?
rationale: The requested behavior intentionally changes the documented lifecycle contract and introduces a decision about whether Workboard may authoritatively evaluate external review and merge state.

options.title: Strengthen evidence without fail-closing
options.body: Keep manual acceptance of `done`, improve structured proof and diagnostics, and let GitHub or other higher-level workflows remain authoritative for review and integration.

options.title: Define bounded plugin gates
options.body: Adopt narrowly specified Workboard-only completion invariants, with a documented legacy-card migration and without treating external pull-request state as independently authoritative.

options.title: Adopt full cross-system completion enforcement
options.body: Make Workboard reject completion against proof, dependency, and linked pull-request conditions after maintainers define ownership, verifier contracts, failures, and upgrades.

recommendation.title: Strengthen evidence without fail-closing
recommendation.body: Keep manual acceptance of `done`, improve structured proof and diagnostics, and let GitHub or other higher-level workflows remain authoritative for review and integration.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Workboard lifecycle work makes this the strongest available area-routing signal.
